newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel in free trade with Canada, Slovakia, Czech.
newsitem.headline: Israel in free trade with Canada, Slovakia, Czech.

text.p: Bilateral free-trade agreements between Israel and the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Canada go into effect on Wednesday, Israel's Industry and Trade Ministry said on Tuesday.
The new trade regimes are the result of bilateral agreements signed over the course of the year.

In addition, restrictions from imports from Jordan will be eased. The ministry said 56 new product categories would enjoy full customs exemption, another 50 would qualify for 50 percent reductions and a further 40 for 30 percent reductions.

A fourth free-trade pact, with Turkey, is awaiting approval by Turkey's parliament. The ministry said it expected the vote would take place during January and that the agreement would take effect immediately afterwards.
The trade accord with Canada exempts all industrial products from customs, while agricultural and processed-food products enjoy preferred terms.

"Canada already has a free trade agreement with the United States," the ministry noted. "The new agreement will significantly improve the competitive ability of Israeli exports, especially in telecommunications, plastics, textiles, clothing and food."

The Czech, Slovakian and Turkish accords will immediately exempt a significant portion of industrial exports for customs. Among the exceptions are textile and clothing, on which duties will be reduced gradually to the year 2000.
